clue.text: The ticket of an American president in the fifties

indicators.note: the president is placed inside the pair of fifties, sitting between them

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give two Ls
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, sixteenth president of the United States

explanation.surface: A question about the election ticket of a US president during the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fifties' suggests the decade of Eisenhower; it is really two Roman fifties (L and L) with Lincoln between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket is a tag or tie-on slip, the same thing as a label.

clue.text: Cosmetics used with boldness and craft to hide mark

parts.note: lip means cheek, impudent boldness

indicators.note: the craft conceal the mark by enclosing it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship; craft here are ships
a tick is a mark made on paper

explanation.surface: Makeup applied with daring and skill to conceal a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipsticks are sticks of colour applied to the lips, a type of makeup.

clue.text: Lawyers say set up water-transport

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are turned to read upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Barristers propose setting up a canal service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns EG (say, for example) into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed boat for carrying goods on rivers and canals.

clue.text: Sort of cover-up that makes many a politician colour

parts.note: L, the Roman fifty, stands for many in crosswords
MP is a Member of Parliament
a shade is a colour or hue

explanation.surface: A political scandal-hush that makes many politicians blush.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampshade covers a bulb, a cover-up of a literal kind.

clue.text: When choreographed, the dances must be disciplined

indicators.note: when dance steps are choreographed they are arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dancers are told that once the routine is set they must behave themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When choreographed' rearranges THE DANCES; 'When' and 'must be' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be chastened is to be humbled and corrected, i.e. punished into better behaviour.

clue.text: Prudence's admonition

explanation.surface: A woman named Prudence giving someone a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Caution means carefulness, and also a formal warning, as police give.

clue.text: Entertainer giving the painter a key

parts.note: a painter is an artist
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A performer passes a painter a key.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Like to put up her name?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
to set is to put down

explanation.surface: Asking whether to post up a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a girl's name, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Clothing produced specially for retired people is treated with anger

definitions.text: Clothing produced specially for retired people

indicators.note: the letters are processed, worked over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Garments made for pensioners get an angry reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' means gone to bed, not stopped working; 'is treated' rearranges WITH ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is pyjamas and nightdresses, worn by people who have gone to bed.

clue.text: Spot the lady's admirer

parts.note: a dot is a spot
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Pointing out a woman's suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A doter is someone who dotes, a fond admirer.

clue.text: The average sum is of the utmost importance

parts.note: par is the normal or average standard, as in 'below par'
an amount is a sum, as of money

explanation.surface: A statement that the mean total matters above all else.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount describes something supreme, ranking above everything else.

clue.text: There's a great deal to see

explanation.surface: A promise of plenty of attractions for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight means a lot, as in 'a sight better'; and to sight something is to spot it.

clue.text: A little actress in a plait

indicators.note: only a small part of the word actress is taken, the last five letters

explanation.surface: A small performer wearing her hair braided.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock of hair, often worn braided or plaited.

clue.text: This may be transient, but right now

indicators.note: the word transient may be turned into this one by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Something fleeting that nevertheless is happening this very minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' stands for the answer: rearranged, its letters may become TRANSIENT, read the other way as an anagram of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is an old legal word for immediately, at once.

clue.text: Officer in the army wearing peaked hat at the front

indicators.note: the hat goes before the rest of the wordplay, at the start

parts.note: a cap is a hat with a peak
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier with a peaked cap is identified as an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time reserve; 'wearing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in the army, and in the navy too.

clue.text: A dangerous example of creeping inflation in Africa

definitions.text: A dangerous example of creeping inflation in Africa

parts.words: A dangerous example of creeping inflation in Africa
parts.note: sounds like economics, but means a venomous snake that crawls and swells itself up when threatened

explanation.definitionFit: The puff adder is a venomous African viper that inflates its body when alarmed.

clue.text: Happening to carry the same manifest

indicators.note: the happening holds the second piece within it, carrying it inside

parts.note: an event is a happening
ID is short for idem, Latin for the same, used in references

explanation.surface: An occurrence that carries the same message as a declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest as an adjective means plainly visible or obvious.

clue.text: Move in units divided about military honour and, create friction

indicators.note: the two units are split apart, set either side of the honour

parts.note: I is one, a unit, so units give two Is
MM is the Military Medal
to grate is to rub harshly, creating friction

explanation.surface: Moving into army units that are split over a medal causes friction.
explanation.definitionFit: To immigrate is to come into a country to settle there.

clue.text: Exceptionally clear note showing open-mindedness

indicators.note: an exceptional treatment of the letters puts them out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An unusually clear musical note shows broad sympathies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is a willingness to accept views that differ from one's own.

clue.text: Goes through brooks

explanation.surface: Someone wading through streams.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through hardship is to undergo it; to brook something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Think to sit with a little drink first

indicators.note: the drink is placed first, ahead of the sitting

parts.note: a sup is a small mouthful of drink
to pose is to sit, as for a portrait

explanation.surface: Advice to have a quick drink before modelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or believe.

clue.text: Almost idolise a local leader, a top man

indicators.note: almost the whole word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to idolise someone is to admire them greatly

indicators.note: the leader of the word local is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone nearly worships a local headman, treating him as a big chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts ADMIRE to ADMIR; 'leader' takes L from 'local'.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a naval officer of the highest rank, a commander at the top.

clue.text: Cold wind direction

parts.note: Auster is the south wind in classical poetry
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A forecast of chilly wind from some quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: Auster is the Roman name for the south wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and stern, cold in manner.

clue.text: Water-colour pictures?

parts.note: read not as paintings in watercolour but as pictures whose subject is water, the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Seascapes are paintings depicting the sea, literally pictures in which water is coloured.

clue.text: A way to beat the band

parts.note: St is street, a way
to rap is to strike or beat

explanation.surface: A way to outdo a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a strip or band of leather.

clue.text: Warning about royal grave

indicators.note: the warning goes around the royal letter

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, a schoolboy warning
R stands for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: An alarm raised about a king's tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' is a verb here: to engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: To grave is an old verb meaning to engrave, cut into a surface.

clue.text: Individual embraced by king — he's beyond recovery

indicators.note: the individual is held inside the king's letters, hugged by them

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A man held by the king, past saving.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone doomed or past help, sure to die.

clue.text: Involved in a service in Scotland

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the two short words are mixed up

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone taking part in military service north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a church service but is the Royal Navy; Nairn is a town on the Moray Firth in the Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairn is a town in the Scottish Highlands, a place located in that country.

clue.text: Such a comment will get a person up!

definitions.text: Such a comment will get a person up!

parts.words: Such a comment will get a person up!
parts.note: an added remark tacked on to a statement, and also someone who gets up onto a horse

explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an appended clause or remark; it is also someone mounted on a horse or bike.

clue.text: Relation in public performance

indicators.note: the relation is placed inside the word for public

parts.note: open means public, available to all
a ratio is a relation between two quantities

explanation.surface: Kinship displayed in a show before an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a performance of a procedure, the carrying out of a task.

clue.text: French family-man accepting cut to keep going

indicators.note: the father takes the cut into himself, so it sits inside

parts.note: pere is French for father
to sever is to cut

explanation.surface: A French father puts up with a pay cut so he can carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist, continuing despite difficulty.

clue.text: A fellow's obvious hesitation that is without point

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the point stands outside, ahead of the remaining letters

parts.note: er is the sound of someone audibly hesitating
N, north, is a point of the compass
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A man noticeably stammers, as if he has nothing to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside: N stands outside (before) IE. Ernie is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a male first name, so it names one particular man.
